h1:
Freshwater Fish Along the Pa Sak River
Eat with a View
intro: The Pa Sak River runs through Saraburi all the way from Saoi down to Pa Sak Jolasid Dam in Wang Muang, making the whole stretch prime territory for riverside restaurants where you can eat fresh river fish with a cool breeze and wide-open water views. We've pulled together 8 spots that locals actually go to — from floating-raft houses in town to grilled-fish-and-prawn places right on the dam embankment.

blocks.html: Ask someone what to eat in Saraburi and they'll probably say curry puffs from Saoi or fresh milk from Muak Lek first. But the thing locals actually plan meals around is a spread of river fish along the Pa Sak. Order tod mun pla krai, sour curry with cha-om and egg, fried tilapia — then sit on a floating platform or a riverside pavilion with the breeze coming off the water. If you drive further up toward Wang Muang, Pa Sak Jolasid Dam opens things up even more, with grilled fish and river prawn spots right on the water's edge.

blocks.text: What to Order at a Pa Sak River Restaurant

blocks.html: The usual lineup at Pa Sak riverside spots includes pla krai (featherback), tilapia, Nile tilapia, and river prawns. Each restaurant has its own strengths — some shine with fried dishes, others with sour curry. Here's what's worth ordering.

items: Tod mun pla krai (featherback fish cakes) — the Pa Sak signature. Chewy and springy, pressed flat and fried, served with cucumber relish.
Fried tilapia with garlic / luay suan (fresh herb salad) — good-sized fish, firm flesh, crispy skin with soft interior. Comes with dipping sauce or a fresh vegetable salad.
Gaeng som cha-om kai / gaeng som kung (sour curry with vegetables or prawns) — bold, forward sourness. The dish most people reorder. Best eaten with a bowl of hot steamed rice.
Salt-grilled fish / pla nin pao (grilled Nile tilapia) — the dam-zone staple. Whole fish grilled until the skin crisps up, pulled apart and dipped in seafood sauce.
Grilled river prawns — the headline item around Pa Sak Dam. Big, full of roe, priced by size and season — ask before you order.

blocks.text: 8 Riverside Fish Restaurants Locals Actually Visit

items.name: Tom Khwae Pa Sak
items.blurb: The long-standing floating-raft restaurant on the Pa Sak River in Saoi, open for over 20 years. Seating covers both the riverbank and actual floating platforms mid-river, with a wide-open view and a steady breeze. The standouts are the chewy tod mun pla krai and a punchy gaeng som with small river shrimp. Prices are approachable — dishes run 80–350 THB — and this is the go-to spot when locals want a proper family meal on the water.

items.name: Chao Khuen Restaurant
items.blurb: A riverside spot on the Wang Muang side of Pa Sak Jolasid Dam, just before the dam entrance. The dining area is open and airy with a good cross-breeze. The draw here is large grilled river prawns loaded with roe, alongside river fish cooked in a dam-side style. Good timing: come when you're already visiting the dam or if you're there during the flood season to watch the 'floating train' pass over the reservoir.

items.name: Mint River & Restaurant
items.blurb: A chill riverside spot right on the Pa Sak in downtown Saraburi, with live music most nights. Good for a long, relaxed evening meal with a drink in hand and the river breeze coming through. The menu mixes river fish with standard Thai dishes and bar snacks.

items.name: Samrap Lao
items.blurb: An Isan-style restaurant by the Pa Sak River — the right pick if you want bold, spicy flavors over a scenic setting. Order river fish done as larb or koi, pad fish sauce, and pair it with som tum and sticky rice while the river air keeps things comfortable.
items.meta: Pa Sak riverside · Authentic Isan cooking

items.name: Thara Dining Room
items.blurb: A Thai restaurant on a sizeable stream, focused on fresh freshwater fish done in classic Saraburi style. Open from morning through evening, making it a solid choice for a midday family meal — you eat to the sound of running water and walk away genuinely cool.

items.name: Krua Pla Sarawut
items.blurb: The name tells you exactly what they care about: fish. The menu covers freshwater fish in all its forms — fried, steamed, curried — at reasonable prices. Well-known among downtown Saraburi locals. Good call if you want serious fish dishes without paying for a premium water view.

items.name: Krua Kung Luang, Pa Sak Dam
items.blurb: Another dam-zone spot with a name that leans into its prawn credentials. Order grilled prawns or glass-noodle-baked prawns alongside river fish, in an open breezy setting. Works well as a meal after exploring the dam or just before heading back.
items.meta: Pa Sak Dam zone · Prawn-forward menu

items.name: Lan Rim Nam Muak Lek
items.blurb: A shaded riverside spot in the Muak Lek area, right on the water. A natural stop if you've been visiting the Muak Lek waterfalls and want a relaxed meal with some shade and greenery. Standard Thai food and fish on the menu, easy scenery.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: River fish and prawns are priced by size and weight, and rates shift with the season. Before you order, ask for the weight and the per-kilo price so there are no surprises on the bill. Most riverside spots get busy on weekend evenings — if you're coming as a group, call ahead to reserve a table on the water.

blocks.text: How to Pick the Right Spot

items.name: Want a floating raft in town
items.blurb: Go to Tom Khwae Pa Sak in Saoi — actual floating platforms on the Pa Sak River, a full fish menu, and prices that don't hurt.

items.name: Want a wide-open dam view
items.blurb: Drive up to Wang Muang and hit Chao Khuen or Krua Kung Luang. Big grilled river prawns, horizon-to-horizon water.

items.name: Want spicy food by the river
items.blurb: Head to Samrap Lao. Order larb fish, koi, som tum, sticky rice — Isan-style all the way, with the Pa Sak breeze as a bonus.

blocks.html: Late afternoon heading into sunset is when riverside restaurants look their best — the light drops, the air cools, and the water catches the reflection. The dam zone gets especially lively from late rainy season into early cool season (around November–January), when the 'floating train' runs across the reservoir and visitors pour in. Dam-side restaurants fill up fast during this window — either arrive early or call ahead.

blocks.title: Getting Here by Car
blocks.html: The Pa Sak riverside restaurants in downtown Saraburi and Saoi are easy to reach — nothing complicated from the town center. The Pa Sak Dam zone in Wang Muang is about 40–50 minutes further, with a bit of winding hill road toward the end. Build in extra time and fill your tank before leaving town.

faq.q: Which riverside restaurant on the Pa Sak River in Saraburi is the most well-known?
faq.a: Tom Khwae Pa Sak in Saoi is the long-standing floating-raft institution that locals know best — open for over 20 years, famous for its chewy tod mun pla krai and tangy gaeng som with small river shrimp, with seating both on the bank and on actual floating platforms.

faq.q: Where should I go for grilled river prawns near Pa Sak Dam?
faq.a: Chao Khuen Restaurant and Krua Kung Luang are both in the Pa Sak Jolasid Dam zone on the Wang Muang side, and both are known for their large grilled river prawns. Open setting, good breeze, wide water view — ideal after exploring the dam.

faq.q: How much does a meal at a Pa Sak riverside restaurant cost?
faq.a: Restaurants in town and in Saoi typically run 80–350 THB per dish, working out to roughly 200–500 THB per person. Dam-side spots focused on river prawns run higher depending on size and season — expect around 300–600 THB per person.

faq.q: What freshwater fish dishes should I order?
faq.a: Tod mun pla krai, fried tilapia with garlic, gaeng som with cha-om and egg or with prawns. If you're at the dam zone, don't skip the salt-grilled Nile tilapia and the grilled river prawns.

faq.q: Is Pa Sak Jolasid Dam in Saraburi or Lopburi?
faq.a: The reservoir straddles both provinces — the Saraburi side is in Wang Muang District, while the main dam face sits on the Lopburi side. Riverside restaurants exist on both sides, so you can choose whichever is easier to reach from your route.
